A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VJA, IESBench, and introspective-defense work. All 27 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack and defense evaluations on IESBench, human–model judge comparisons, sensitivity experiments, and qualitative failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds judge–human agreement statistics and defense-generalization results in Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: Section 2.2 emphasizes KV-cache reuse, which v1 already described and illustrated in Figure 3. The safety trigger and defense procedure remain the same; Appendix A.6 applies the defense to additional backbones without documenting a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,054-image IESBench, risk categories, editing tasks, and visual-prompt sensitivity scenarios. The additional defense backbones do not introduce new datasets, populations, or task requirements.

E2.justification: The TJA comparison and five MLLM judge models are retained. Table 7 extends the existing with/without-defense comparison to additional backbones, using the same undefended control condition without introducing a competing attack or defense method.

E3.justification: Appendix A.5 adds Pearson correlation and Kappa as judge-validation metrics. Appendix A.6 adds paired defense-on/off evaluations for LongCat-Image and Flux2.0[dev]. Existing evaluation settings remain unchanged; sample selection for the new analyses is not specified.

E4.justification: New Appendices A.5–A.6 provide focused extensions examining judge–human consistency and defense transfer across backbones. Existing reasoning ablations, visual-prompt sensitivity tests, computational analysis, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Table 6 introduces Pearson correlation and Kappa estimates of agreement with human judgments. The five repetitions reported for Figure 7 and the uncertainty reporting in Table 3 are unchanged; no additional seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests are reported.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports agreement scores, including Gemini 3 Pro's Pearson/Kappa values of 0.79/0.67. New Table 7 reports ASR reductions from 100.0% to 71.9% for LongCat-Image and to 69.0% for Flux2.0[dev], alongside HS, EV, and HRR results. Existing results remain unchanged; the new experiments' incompletely specified settings prevent direct comparison with earlier baseline scores.

T1.justification: The attack formalization and metric equations (1)–(5) retain their mathematical substance. Section 2.2 removes an inline prompt-concatenation shorthand, but introduces no revised formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about visual jailbreaks, IESBench, and an efficient training-free defense. The appendix additions support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 interprets the new agreement estimates as supporting the default Gemini judge. Appendix A.6 explicitly argues that defense transfer is applicable to models with language-space safety alignment. Existing limitations concerning visual understanding and misleading information remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 revises technical model descriptions, notably removing the assertion that GPT Image 1.5 uses a native multimodal architecture within a single neural network. Hardware, API usage, prompt enhancement, and access information remain unchanged; implementation details for the new defense transfers are not added.

R1.justification: The Google Cloud Veo 3.1 prompting-guide citation is replaced by Fortin et al.'s Veo 3.1/Gemini API announcement. Broader research positioning and prior-benchmark comparisons remain unchanged; other reference edits mainly concern formatting or metadata.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized defense-description and rubric edits, corrects author information, adds acknowledgments, and inserts two appendix subsections. The earlier benchmark-comparison subsection becomes A.7. The overall narrative and section structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–7 and reflows the subsequent appendix material. The existing model-information table becomes Table 8 and moves to page 27. Existing figures and qualitative examples are retained, including Figure 12's visually present labels.

improvement.justification: Tables 6–7 modestly strengthen validation of the judge and defense portability beyond the largely Qwen-focused efficacy evidence in v1. These additions improve empirical support without changing the core results. The benefit is limited by unspecified sampling and integration details, and by unexplained differences between newly reported baseline scores and retained results.
